blogs.title: Bridging Vessels, Not Ovaries: Diagnosing Pedunculated Fibroids That Mimic Adnexal Cysts in Pregnancy
blogs.description: When a massive “ovarian cyst” is actually a pedunculated, cystically degenerating fibroid, getting the diagnosis right prevents overtreatment. This post walks through the bedside bimanual exam, ultrasound clues (bridging-vessel sign, continuity with the uterus), and non-contrast MRI hallmarks (claw sign, myometrial continuity) that distinguish fibroids from decidualized endometriomas. We also highlight how degeneration alters T1/T2 signals, why CA-125 can mislead in pregnancy, and a pragmatic imaging algorithm that avoids gadolinium.

blogs.title: Second-Trimester Myomectomy for Torsion and Mass Effect: Doing the Minimum Necessary
blogs.description: Myomectomy in pregnancy is usually avoided, but torsion, leakage, infection risk, or relentless pain/dyspnoea justify action. Using this case, we outline clear indications, why pedunculated lesions are the safest targets, and the value of a deliberately limited operation: control the stalk, close the base, minimize uterine manipulation, and leave intramural masses in situ. We discuss approach selection (laparotomy vs laparoscopy), hemostatic tactics, counselling on preterm risks, and how targeted surgery can rapidly reverse restrictive mechanics.

blogs.title: Nonobstetric Surgery in Pregnancy: A Practical Perioperative Playbook at 20–24 Weeks
blogs.description: From consent to closure, this is a concise checklist for safe second-trimester surgery. Pre-op: document fetal cardiac activity, optimize anemia, plan VTE prophylaxis, and align antibiotics with pregnancy-safe options. Intra-op: left lateral tilt, avoid hypotension/hypoxemia, use intermittent fetal assessment when previable, and keep operative time short. Post-op: individualized tocolysis only if contractions arise (prophylactic progesterone has uncertain benefit), multimodal analgesia that avoids late-gestation NSAID exposure, and clear triggers for obstetric re-evaluation.

blogs.title: Birth Planning With Large Fibroids: Vaginal Trial or Elective Caesarean?
blogs.description: Route of delivery hinges on size, number, and location—not just the word “fibroid.” We review how posterior and lower-segment masses can obstruct descent, why interval growth trends matter, and when elective caesarean at 37 weeks can reduce maternal–fetal risk. We also address the CS-myomectomy debate (who benefits, hemorrhage mitigation strategies) and how postpartum regression plus symptom trajectory inform shared decisions about deferred surgery.

blogs.title: Interpreting CA-125 in Pregnancy: Trends, Traps, and When to Worry
blogs.description: CA-125 naturally varies across trimesters and rises with many benign conditions, including endometriosis and fibroids, making single values treacherous. This post reviews expected ranges by trimester, how to use serial trends alongside imaging, and red flags that should still prompt oncologic review. The takeaway: don’t let a mildly elevated CA-125 drive an aggressive operation when anatomy and imaging point to a benign myomatous process.

blogs.title: Short of Breath From Below: Recognizing Restrictive Mechanics From Giant Pelvic Masses in Pregnancy
blogs.description: Dyspnoea in pregnancy isn’t always cardiopulmonary. We outline how massive subphrenic or uterine-adjacent lesions create true restrictive physiology, how to separate this from physiologic dyspnoea, and why semi-orthostatic positioning and targeted analgesia can help temporize. The post discusses safe diagnostic steps, when symptom escalation should trigger decompression, and how rapid relief after limited myomectomy validates a mechanical cause.
